title: Immutability
description: Learn why immutability matters in Redux and how to achieve it.

data.text: **Immutability** means never modifying data directly. In Redux, you must always return a new object from a reducer instead of mutating the existing one. This single rule is what makes Redux predictable and powers features like time-travel debugging and fast reference equality checks.

data.title: Never Mutate State
data.text: Mutating state directly breaks Redux. The UI will not re-render correctly, DevTools will not work, and time-travel debugging becomes impossible. Always return a new object.

data.title: Benefits
items: **Predictability**: State changes are traceable through the action log
**Performance**: React-Redux can skip re-renders using `===` comparison
**Time-Travel**: Keep a history of states to jump between them
**Debugging**: Easier to find the action that caused a bug
**Concurrency**: Safe to share state across contexts because it never changes unexpectedly

cards.title: Mutating (Bad)
cards.description: Directly modifying the existing state object. Breaks Redux's contract.

cards.title: Immutable (Good)
cards.description: Returning a new object with the updated values. Preserves the previous state.
cards.code:
return { ...state, count: state.count + 1 };
return { ...state, items: [...state.items, newItem] };

data.title: Spread Operator Basics
data.content: Use the spread operator to create new objects and arrays

data.text: Deeply nested state is common, and updating it immutably requires spreading at every level along the path. This can feel verbose, which is why Redux Toolkit uses Immer to let you write 'mutating' code that is actually immutable under the hood.

data.title: Redux Toolkit + Immer
data.text: Redux Toolkit's createSlice uses Immer internally. You can write 'mutating' code like `state.value += 1`, but Immer produces a new immutable state for you. This is the modern, recommended approach.

terms.definition: The property that data is never modified after creation. Updates always produce new values.
The `...` syntax that copies the enumerable properties of an object or array into a new one.
Comparison using `===` that checks whether two values point to the same object in memory.
A library that lets you write mutating code while producing immutable updates under the hood. Used by Redux Toolkit.

data.title: Convert to Immutable
data.description: Given a mutating reducer, rewrite it to be fully immutable using only spread and array methods.
steps: Identify every place state is being mutated
Rewrite each line to return a new object or array
Verify by adding a console.log of `state` inside the reducer to confirm the original is not changed
data.expectedOutcome: A working reducer that produces the same behavior but never mutates the input state. The console should show the previous state is preserved after each action.

Key Takeaways
points: Redux requires all state updates to be immutable
Use spread and array methods (map, filter) to create new values
Spread at every level of a nested path
Reference equality enables fast re-render checks in React-Redux
Redux Toolkit's Immer integration removes most of this boilerplate
data.takeaway: Immutability is the foundation that makes Redux predictable, performant, and time-travel friendly.
